title: Structure and substrate recognition by the Twin-arginine translocation (Tat) pathway core complex
authors: Deme JC; Bryant Oj; Batista M; Stansfeld PJ; Berks BC; Lea SM
one_liner_zh: 该文研究Tat转运系统核心复合物的结构与底物识别机制，对象为膜蛋白转运复合物而非无序蛋白/IDR，虽涉及蛋白-蛋白互作和结构解析，但无AI/物理模拟方法，对无序蛋白互作机制建模的启发有限。
abstract: The twin-arginine translocation (Tat) system is a mechanistically unique protein transport pathway moving folded proteins across membranes (1-4). It is found in all domains of life and is essential for plant photosynthesis and bacterial virulence(2, 5-7). A core complex composed of membrane proteins TatA, TatB, and TatC binds substrate proteins and then recruits additional TatA protomers to form the transport site(8-10). Here we present structures of resting and substrate-bound states of the Tat core complex together with biochemical and functional analysis. Substrate proteins associate with the core complex solely through their N-terminal signal peptides with their Tat targeting sequences making specific contacts with TatC and the peptide body clamped by TatB. The core complex contains highly tilted transmembrane helices that drive extreme local membrane thinning. Based on our results we propose a model for the early steps in Tat transport.
abstract_zh: 双精氨酸转运（Tat）系统是一种机制独特的蛋白质转运途径，能够将折叠蛋白跨膜运输（1-4）。该系统存在于所有生命域中，对植物光合作用和细菌致病性至关重要（2, 5-7）。由膜蛋白TatA、TatB和TatC组成的核心复合物结合底物蛋白，随后招募额外的TatA原体以形成转运位点（8-10）。在此，我们展示了Tat核心复合物在静息态和底物结合态的结构，并结合了生化和功能分析。底物蛋白仅通过其N端信号肽与核心复合物结合，其中Tat靶向序列与TatC发生特异性接触，而肽体部分则由TatB夹持。核心复合物含有高度倾斜的跨膜螺旋，这些螺旋驱动局部膜显著变薄。基于我们的结果，我们提出了Tat转运早期步骤的模型。
